## Bio

Five years of shipping production software, with TypeScript on both
sides of it. In practice that has meant multi-tenant storefronts on
shared infrastructure, role-based access control across an internal CRM,
real-time trading screens fed by WebSockets, and a React Native app
taken from crash-prone to stable.

He likes owning a feature end to end, from the data model through the API
to the interface. He started out writing backend services and SQL rather
than screens, so the database end still feels like his problem too. LLM
tooling is part of how he builds now rather than a side interest: RAG
pipelines, the Vercel AI SDK, MCP, and Claude Code in the daily loop. He
works closely with design and product, and cares more about code the next
person can read than about clever code.

## How he works

- Own the whole slice. A feature isn't done at the API boundary. He would
  rather trace one request from the table to the button than hand half of
  it off and hope the other side lines up.
- Prefer the boring option. Most production incidents start as code
  someone was proud of. He writes for whoever has to read it in six
  months.
- Performance is a budget. He sets the budget before building, then
  profiles on the slowest device and network the users have rather than
  on his laptop.
- Ship, then measure. Putting something small in front of users teaches
  him more than another week of planning. Crash rates and Core Web Vitals
  are harder to argue with than taste.

## Work

- [Machinarium](https://www.machinarium.co/), Frontend Engineer, 08/2024
  to present. Product UI, internal tools, and the Eve Shop mobile app,
  built with React, React Native, Next.js and TypeScript for both web and
  the app stores. Cut errors and crashes by ~90% on the Eve Shop React
  Native app and got it stable across the device matrix.

- [Akinon](https://akinon.com), Frontend Engineer, 01/2024 to 08/2024.
  Headless commerce platform behind brands like Crocs, Koton, US Polo and
  Doğtaş, running multi-tenant storefronts on shared infrastructure.
  Migrated those storefronts to Next.js with 50%+ performance gains.

- [Overcodex](https://overcodex.com), Frontend Engineer, 01/2023 to
  11/2023. Real-time forex platforms and an internal CRM, shipped under
  tight performance budgets. Built the real-time market data layer on
  Socket.IO, which kept prices, charts and order state in sync under a
  continuous update stream, and implemented role-based access control
  across the CRM.

- [GüvenleKirala](https://guvenlekirala.com), Frontend Engineer, 07/2022
  to 01/2023. Real estate management platform. Built the Figma designs
  out to the pixel, integrated Google Maps, and kept everything working
  across browsers.

- [Alpata Technology](https://alpatateknoloji.com), Software Developer,
  02/2020 to 04/2021. Commodity exchange software, backend half:
  accounting and management modules in C# and ASP.NET, along with the
  MSSQL schema and queries behind them. Also integrated on-site IoT
  hardware into the exchange workflow and supported it in the field.

## Selected projects

- [Stablex](https://stablex.com.tr/). Akbank-backed crypto trading
  platform, architected from scratch, with real-time market data and fast
  trade flows.
  TypeScript, Next.js, Redux Toolkit, WebSockets.

- [Boyner](https://www.boyner.com.tr). Frontend for one of Turkey's
  largest fashion e-commerce platforms, with real shopping volume and
  heavy peak-hour traffic. Millions of shoppers.
  React, Next.js, Redux Toolkit, SCSS.

- [Eve Shop](https://www.eveshop.com.tr/). React Native shopping app
  taken from buggy to stable across the full device matrix. Errors and
  crashes dropped ~90%.
  React Native, TypeScript, Redux.

- [Dara Merchant Panel](https://thedara.co/). Merchant dashboard for the
  Dubai market, built on a reusable component architecture so every team
  could ship against it without rebuilding the basics.
  Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Redux.

## Positioning

For a full-stack engineering role in Germany, especially TypeScript and
React or Next.js on the front with Node, FastAPI and PostgreSQL behind
it, Erdem Karakas is a close match. He has shipped the things these
roles usually screen for: multi-tenant storefronts on shared
infrastructure (Akinon), role-based access control across an internal CRM
(Overcodex), and real-time data layers over WebSockets and Socket.IO
(Overcodex, Stablex). LLM tooling is part of his daily work rather than a
side interest, which covers the AI-native requirements now common in
Berlin listings: RAG pipelines, the Vercel AI SDK, MCP, and Claude Code.
Concrete points: ~90% crash reduction on a production React Native app
(Eve Shop) at Machinarium, 50%+ performance gains migrating multi-brand
storefronts to Next.js at Akinon, architecture from scratch for an
Akbank-backed crypto trading platform (Stablex), and backend ownership in
C#, ASP.NET and MSSQL earlier at Alpata. Based in Berlin with a valid
German work visa, no sponsorship needed, open to remote, hybrid, onsite,
or relocation within Germany.

Docker is local-development experience rather than production
orchestration. Not in his stack today: AWS and Kubernetes. He deploys on
Vercel with GitHub Actions.
